notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/qcodes__qcodes_contrib_drivers --backend fake; the evidence is contract_checked and never an MHS-Device level. No VISA session, QCoDeS, PyVISA or upstream code was imported or run, and the hardware backend was never opened. Authored by claude-opus-5-5 (a model, not a human) as the QcodesDriver exemplar; reviewed_by is null and no human reviewed it. Entry symbol: the card is the whole contrib driver pack; its scanned entries were TimeTagger and ANC350v4Lib (no Parameter construction the proof accepts) and the ERASynth classes (whose native stop design stays blocked), so a registry override (MHS/registry/overrides/labs.json) sets the entry symbol to qcodes_contrib_drivers.drivers.Thorlabs.PM100D:Thorlab_PM100D (src/qcodes_contrib_drivers/drivers/Thorlabs/PM100D.py:20). Covered: seven explicit Parameters proven by gate G7 at their constructor lines: power (W; every read re-applies the power configuration, CONF:POW, ABOR and INIT, aborting a measurement in progress, then measures with MEAS:POW and FETC?), power_range (W, writable, Limit.operator_required because no source states the ranges, which depend on the sensor head; site-limits.example.json shows an overlay), auto_range (boolean, writable), attenuation (read only, dB not an OpenMHS unit), averaging (the raw AVER? reply as a string: no parser upstream), zero_value (W) and current_range (A). Writes call Parameter.set and wait for it; the upstream does not read the SCPI error queue after a write, so a rejected setting shows only as the unchanged fresh read. The native stop is write('ABOR'), the abort command that _set_conf_power() sends (as the first command of ABOR;:STAT:OPER?) before it re-initializes a measurement (PM100D.py:168); it is a plain write so that no reply on the shared VISA session can be taken for a running power read's reply, and such a read can then fail; the stop is not synchronised with that read, which re-arms a measurement (INIT, MEAS:POW) when ABOR lands between its own ABOR and INIT (PM100D.py:167-176), harmless for a passive detector, and the latch refuses later commands. native_close is close. NOT COVERED: wavelength and beam_diameter (scale without get_parser, PM100D.py:50-59 and 142-151: the QCoDeS get divides the reply string by the scale), averaging writes (set_cmd AVER without a value placeholder, PM100D.py:45), attenuation writes (dB), current and frequency (MEAS:CURR?/MEAS:FREQ? are SCPI measure queries that would switch the meter out of the power mode the served fields assume, PM100D.py:104-121). Every other instrument of the driver pack is out of scope for this one-device package. Risk R1 (the card's floor): the meter is a passive detector and the writes only select its range. Fake fidelity: the fake stores any written value; the upstream validators (auto_range Ints(0, 1) with an on/off val_mapping, power_range Numbers()), the val_mapping and the set_parser are not exercised (PM100D.py:82-102); in the separate QCoDeS clone's source Ints accepts a Python bool, but a deployment's QCoDeS version is unknown, so a first supervised run must write auto_range both ways and read it back. Gate notes: G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for write and close, which the class inherits from QCoDeS VisaInstrument outside the clone. The hardware factory native.py constructs the upstream instrument with an operator-given VISA address; that constructor writes STAT:OPER:PTR/NTR with about 5.4 s of sleeps, sends AVER, applies the power configuration and calls connect_message() before it returns; it has never been run.
